designPrinciple: A beginner first receives a bounded explanation or demonstration, predicts and traces behavior, then writes, compiles with warnings, breaks safely, repairs from evidence, verifies, explains, and proves a progressively less scaffolded modern C++ program.
targetLearner: A tertiary fresher or independent beginner with basic computer literacy and no assumed programming experience
technologySequence: Windows g++/GDB and VS Code setup
source, compilation, main, output streams, typed fixed values, and diagnostics
std::getline, istringstream, full-consumption parsing, ranges, and ordered decisions
loops, std::vector, size, counters, accumulators, and safe summaries
function contracts, values, const references, namespaces, headers, translation units, and linker evidence
classes, constructors, private invariants, bounded exceptions, automatic lifetime, and value ownership
standard algorithms, iterators, narrow lambdas, explicit capture, and std::map summaries
file streams, candidate writes, rollback, debugger evidence, and dependency-free checks
argc/argv, modular CLI integration, Git, README, and GitHub
learningRhythm: active prediction, compile, run, trace, or precise reference
required Build in sessions of at most two hours

resourceRoleStrategy.learn: A short first explanation or visual demonstration.
resourceRoleStrategy.practice: An observable prediction, compile, run, trace, debugger inspection, or comparison.
resourceRoleStrategy.reference: A precise bounded language, compiler, or library lookup beside immediate work, never an unscoped documentation dump.

progressionPolicy: Weeks 1-3 establish compilation, diagnostics, full-line validation, decisions, loops, and vectors without a calculator-first jump.
Weeks 4-7 combine earlier syntax through functions, multi-file builds, classes, value ownership, algorithms, maps, persistence, debugging, and checks.
Week 8 introduces only command-line routing and safe publication while integrating already proven competencies.
workloadPrinciples: Eight instructional Weeks at six hours each.
Setup is separate and skippable only through explicit verification.
No Build session exceeds two hours.
Most time is reserved for writing, compiling, tracing, debugging, checks, evidence, and explanation rather than passive consumption.
assessmentPolicy: Each Week has ten independently authored, source-mapped questions; 7/10 passes; attempts are unlimited; option order reshuffles per attempt; program competence is judged through Build and Proof, not quiz score alone.

projectArchitecture.title: C++ Practice Portfolio
projectArchitecture.outcome: Produce seven progressively stronger warning-clean programs demonstrating execution, validation, decisions, vectors, functions, classes, value ownership, algorithms, persistence, debugging, and checks.

projectArchitecture.title: CoursePilot CLI
projectArchitecture.outcome: Deliver and publish a verified, persistent, source-only modern C++ command-line program with reproducible build instructions and human-reviewable evidence.
